slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Exterior Angle Theorem: an exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles.

Proof: the exterior angle and its adjacent interior angle form a linear pair, so they add to 180. The three interior angles also add to 180. Subtract the adjacent angle from both: the exterior angle equals the sum of the other two. This makes the inequality from 5.2 exact, now that we have the Parallel Postulate.
